name: Detecting Pretraining Data from Large Language Models
problem: LLMs are trained on trillions of tokens, almost certainly including test data for widely reported benchmarks, but there's no way to know which data was included.
mechanism: Introduces WIKIMIA (dynamic benchmark using data created before/after model training) and Min-K% Prob detection method. Min-K% Prob: unseen examples contain outlier words with low probabilities; seen examples don't. Achieves 7.4% improvement on WIKIMIA over previous methods. Applied to copyrighted book detection, contaminated downstream example detection, and privacy auditing.
notes:
arXiv preprint, no venue claim in comments. This is the canonical paper on benchmark contamination detection. The key insight: if a model has seen a benchmark in training, its perplexity on that benchmark will be artificially low, making the benchmark result meaningless. The Min-K% Prob method requires no knowledge of the pretraining corpus.
